core_obligations: Get the equality of the two sets from the algebra criterion for smoothness at a point over a perfect field (proof lines 4741-4744).
Get openness from the openness of the smooth locus of a morphism (proof lines 4744-4746).

Give the two density arguments: the generic points of X lie in the set because their local rings are fields, hence regular; and X is geometrically reduced over a perfect field, so the dense smooth open criterion applies directly (proof lines 4747-4753).
proof_roadmap: Equality of the two sets (proof lines 4741-4744).
difficulty_reason: For a perfect field k and a locally algebraic reduced k-scheme X, the lemma identifies the set of points where X over Spec(k) is smooth with the set of points whose local ring is regular, and shows that this set is a dense open subscheme (statement lines 4729-4738). The proof separates the three claims: the equality of the two sets is a direct consequence of the algebra criterion relating smoothness at a point to separability of the residue field over a perfect field; openness is the openness of the smooth locus; and density is given twice, once through the generic points of X, whose local rings are fields and hence regular, and once by combining the geometric reducedness of X over a perfect field with the dense smooth open criterion proved just before (proof lines 4740-4753). The claim is H2: three separate claims, each settled by a standard input, with the double argument for density reflecting the two available routes, and no step referred to the reader beyond the cited immediate consequence.
